findings.evidence: Every other bottleneck explanation in this batch rules out each distractor. Here the learner who picked spam gets no reason. The sends also go out one at a time, which contradicts 'all leave at once'.
findings.old: A provider rate limit can bite as well, and a worker can pace the sends to stay under it.
findings.new: A provider rate limit can bite as well, and a worker can pace the sends to stay under it. Spam filters judge the sender and the content, not whether one request sent the messages, and here they go out one at a time anyway.

findings.problem: The explanation does not address the connection-pool or browser distractors.
findings.evidence: Holding a connection while a huge result streams out is real, so a learner can think option 3 is also right. The explanation should frame it as a symptom of the same volume. It should also say the browser only receives the filtered month.

findings.new: Comparing dates is trivial; it is the volume that hurts. A connection held while all those rows stream out is a symptom of that same volume, not a separate cause, and the browser only ever receives the month that was kept.
